Buy This Bentley Continental GT for the Price of a Toyota Camry and People Will Think You're Loaded
14 photos
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks
If you think that life is too short to spend it driving boring cars but don’t necessarily have the funds to buy a brand-new vehicle with an exciting powertrain capable of neck-snapping performance, wrapped in a luxurious package, then we probably have the right car for you.
We are talking about the Bentley Continental GT pictured above, which may still look brand new to the untrained eye, but those who know a thing or two about cars will recognize that it is a first-gen model. This generation came to life between 2003 and 2011, and for what it’s worth, it has aged like fine wine. This applies to both the exterior and the cockpit, as it still exudes quite modern luxury from its pores.
Beneath the skin lies the old Volkswagen Group D1 platform, and while some might argue that it is nothing more than a Passat with a different body, some chassis tweaks, and a punchy engine under the hood, as well as more premium materials, the truth is that it has nothing in common with the mid-size sedan. But it does with another VW: the Phaeton. The luxury sedan from Volkswagen was made from 2001 and 2016, and this iteration also shared its nuts and bolts with the era’s Audi A8.
We cannot mention the latter without reminding you that production recently ended for good. That’s right, after 32 years, the four-ring brand pulled the plug on its flagship sedan. The last copy was made in mid-October, at the Neckarsulm facility in Germany, so the automaker no longer has a rival to the likes of the Mercedes S-Class and BMW 7 Series.
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks So far, Audi has not confirmed a successor, but those who want a large and quite luxurious Audi can get the first-ever Q9. The full-size SUV takes on the Mercedes GLS and BMW X7, and it is offered in multiple configurations. Unofficial intel suggests that a new flagship sedan might be in the making in China, though details about it are are extremely limited.
Now, back to the pictured Bentley Continental GT, which not only shares its underpinnings with the era’s Audi A8 and Volkswagen Phaeton , but also with the Bentley Flying Spur, which was pretty much a four-door sedan version of its luxury grand tourer sibling.
The GT measured 189.3 inches (4,808 mm) in length, 75.5 inches (1,918 mm) in width, and 54.7 inches (1,390 mm) in height. It had a 108.1 inches (2,746 mm) long wheelbase, and weighed almost 5,200 pounds (2,350 kg).
The pictured car is presented in Moonbeam Silver on top of a Saddle Brown leather interior. It features adaptive, load-leveling air suspension, bi-xenon headlights, an automatic-deploying rear spoiler, heated and power-folding side mirrors, parking sensors at both ends, traction control, electronic stability program, and an electronic differential lock.
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks Other features that are being mentioned in the listing include the 14-way power-adjustable seats at the front with heating and memory settings, a leather-wrapped steering wheel, wood trim, a four-zone automatic climate control system, a 6-disc CD changer, satellite navigation, a premium sound system with 12 speakers, Bluetooth connectivity, cruise control, and a Breitling analog clock, among other things.
Every Bentley fan and their pet can tell you that this generation of the Continental GT was offered strictly with the famous W12 engine. The mill has twin turbos and a 6.0-liter displacement, and pumps out 552 hp (560 ps/412 kW) and 479 pound-feet (650 Nm) of torque. The 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) acceleration was dealt with in less than five seconds, and this model could reach over 198 mph (318 kph) flat out.
Now, the 2005 Bentley Continental GT may not break the bank at all when it comes to the buying part compared to the car that it is, because this thing usually fetches from $18,000 to almost $50,000 in today’s used car market in the States. And we are still talking about a luxury-oriented grand tourer with a punchy engine under the hood aimed at daily drives.
However, just because it does not cost a lot of money to buy does not mean that you should if you are on a tight budget. That’s because it has very high maintenance, and to be honest, it is not exactly the most reliable car out there. Not to mention that it is not frugal either, but you already knew that, didn’t you?
Thus, the last things that we will say about the pictured 2005 Bentley Continental GT are that it has only 6,000 miles (~9,700 km) or so under its belt, which means that it is still new, despite being more than two decades old, and that it costs $38,800. And that’s pretty much new range-topping Toyota Camry money.
Is this luxury GT worth the asking price? If you said yes and want to buy it, then you should reach out to the seller, @diamondmotorworks on Instagram. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Diamond Motorworks (@diamondmotorworks)
